Main quest
MAYN kwest
noun (Gen-Z slang)
The counterpart to side quest in role-playing games: the main quest is the central storyline a player must complete to finish the game. Gen-Z borrowed it in the early 2020s, often alongside main character talk, for the central task of a day or the chief purpose of a life ("okay, back to the main quest").

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

In current slang the main quest is the central task: the thing you are actually supposed to be doing, as opposed to the side quests. It is said of a day ("back to the main quest: laundry"), and sometimes of a life ("what’s even my main quest?"). That second question is a real one, and the culture’s answers are thin: find yourself, chase your dream, get the bag. The Christian observation: Scripture answers it plainly. The Preacher, having tried every side quest under the sun, writes the conclusion: "Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man" (Ecc 12:13). Jesus summed up the law: "Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind" (Mat 22:37). He set the order: "seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you" (Mat 6:33). He gave His church its standing commission: "Go ye therefore, and teach all nations" (Mat 28:19). And Paul lived it as a race with a finish line: "I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus" (Php 3:14). The Westminster Shorter Catechism puts it in one line a child can memorize: man’s chief end is to glorify God, and to enjoy Him for ever. A father tells his son: your job, your marriage, your sport are real quests, but they are not the main one; the main quest was handed to you by your Maker, and its reward is better than anything the game offers.

Webster 1828 Definition

Gen-Z slang (role-playing games; general in the early 2020s) for one’s central task or purpose — a question Scripture answers outright: fear God and keep His commandments, for this is the whole duty of man (Ecc 12:13).

expand to see more

MAIN QUEST, n. (Gen-Z slang, c. 2021–present; gaming origin) One’s central task, as opposed to side quests; one’s chief purpose. "Okay, enough scrolling, back to the main quest."

Often joking about small things (a chore, a test); sometimes earnest about life direction: "I don’t even know what my main quest is."

In role-playing games: the required storyline that leads to the end of the game.

Webster (1828), root word main: “MAIN, adjective [&hellip;] 1. Principal; chief; that which has most power in producing an effect, or which is mostly regarded in prospect; as the main branch or tributary stream of a river; the main timbers of an edifice; a main design; a main object. Our main interest is to be as happy as we can, and as long as possible. 2. Mighty;”

Decode for parents: when your child asks what his main quest is, he is asking the first question of the catechism. Answer it.

Key Scripture

Ecc 12:13 — "Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man."

Mat 22:37 — "Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind."

Mat 6:33 — "But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you."

Mat 28:19 — "Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost:"

Php 3:14 — "I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus."

Modern Corruption

Main quest rightly assumes a life has a central task; the drift is letting the self write it — career, fame, or self-discovery — when the Maker has already given it.

expand to see more

The game metaphor carries a hidden assumption the culture otherwise denies: someone else designed the quest. In a game no player invents the main storyline; he discovers it and follows it. The modern world tells young people to invent their own — to make the career, the following, or the self the main quest — and then wonders why so many feel aimless at twenty-five. The Preacher tried that route, called it vanity, and came at last to "the conclusion of the whole matter" (Ecc 12:13).

Scripture hands out the main quest by name: love God with all the heart, soul, and mind (Mat 22:37); seek first His kingdom (Mat 6:33); make disciples of all nations (Mat 28:19). Every other good thing — work, marriage, children, craft — is a real quest inside that one, and becomes an idol the moment it replaces it. Paul ran his life like a race with one finish line (Php 3:14). Teach your children the catechism early, so that when they ask what life is for, they already know the main quest.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English mægen (strength) → main (chief) + Latin-derived quest (a seeking) → RPG main quest → early-2020s Gen-Z: one’s central task or purpose.
